correctness.rationale: The exact claim is finite and fully quantified: all 2048 binary order-five necklaces, standard lexicographic circular BWT, linear non-wrapping runs. Lemma 1 derives 16 complementary pairs; Lemma 2 gives the LF single-cycle biconditional, grounded in the inspected inversion proof. Formula r=17+#agreements follows by counting within-pair and boundary transitions. Complete integer-only iteration over all 65536 orientations gives the exact counts. A separate exhaustive Euler-tour algorithm independently creates each necklace, directly sorts its rotations, verifies its five-bit windows, and gives exactly the same BWT set and six-bin histogram. Checker run on the actual embedded code passed; no infinite inference, timeout, or unproved nonstandard computational step.

originality.rationale: The Higgins article covers the complementary-block reduction and de Bruijn SET inversion, while the complete one-LF-cycle run histogram remains an additional assertion. Fici et al. 2025 gives only an interval for every order, which at order five is 18..30, strictly weaker than the attained 20..30 and does not imply six multiplicities. The 2025 LFSR preprint constructs special run-minimal patterns, not all order-five sequences. Lipták–Parmigiani counts/constructs de Bruijn sequences, not exact BWT-run class frequencies. Published scholarly-record searches with parameters, phrasing, aliases and numerical array returned no matching or stronger entry. No accessible older own claim includes the exact invariant. Novelty remains a best-knowledge statement subject to historical-table risk.
residual_risks: Historical databases or uninspected documents may contain equivalent order-five six-bin frequency statistics; failed search does not establish absolute novelty.

value.rationale: BWT run number is an established compression and indexing invariant, while de Bruijn cycles are natural maximally diverse test strings. The exact small order-five classification is the first complete nontrivial 2048-necklace regime with six distinct BWT-run outcomes before the order-six family jumps to 67,108,864 necklaces. It refines the existing generic bound by showing that 18 is impossible at this natural order and exactly 38 words attain the true minimum 20; it also determines exact frequencies throughout the range, including only six maximum cases. This natural whole-family exact cutoff is independently useful as a test benchmark for BWT generators and structural conjectures, not an arbitrary slice or a few isolated checks. No all-order theorem is claimed.
